 Judgment

This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed by the appellant/petitioner under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') challenging the judgment and award dated 28.07.2021 passed in MVC No.735/2019 by the I-Additional Senior Civil Judge &
MACT, Kalaburagi (for short, 'the Tribunal') seeking enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4941-DB 2.
Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
Appellant is the petitioner and the respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that on 13.12.2018 at 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding to Humnabad from Fakeertekda in his Goods Auto bearing registration No.KA.39/7498 on left side of the road loaded with old articles, on NH-65 Solapur-Hyderabad road.
When he was near Khaja Hotel, Fakirtekda, a lorry bearing registration No.MH.25/U.4469 came from backside in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the auto.
Due to which, the petitioner sustained multiple fractures all over the body.

Thereafter, he was shifted to United Hospital,
Kalaburagi, wherein he has taken treatment as inpatient from 13.12.2018 to 30.01.2019 and undergone operations and rods were implanted and then he has also taken treatment as inpatient at Gurunanak Hospital, Bidar and undergone operations.

It is contended that the criminal case was Mohd. Rafiq Shah vs Parameshwar And Anr on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193775735/
2 registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.150/2018.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner filed NC: 2024:KHC-K:4941-DB claim petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
4. Respondent No.1 was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It is contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against respondent No.2.
5.
The Tribunal, on the basis of the pleadings of the parties framed relevant issues.
6. The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW.1 and in order to prove the disability, examined the doctor as PW.2 and got marked the 15 documents as Exs.P1 to P15.
The respondents neither lead oral evidence nor documentary evidence.
The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs.
The Tribunal held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,85,250/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

It is also held that respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and the Tribunal directed respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount before the Tribunal within one month from the date of the said judgment and award.
8. The petitioner being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal has filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and also learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.
10.
Learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal NC: 2024:KHC-K:4941-DB under different heads is on the lower side.

He submits that in order to prove the disability, the petitioner has examined the treated doctor as PW.2 who has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of 60% to the whole body whereas the Tribunal has taken the disability at 20% which is on the lower side.
On these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
She submitted the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
On these grounds, she prays to dismiss the appeal.

12. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: The point that arises for our consideration is with regard to quantum of compensation.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner met with an accident and suffered multiple injuries.

In order to prove that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced certified copies of FIR and charge sheet, which are marked as Exs.P1 and P3.
Perusal of Ex.P3 discloses that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in recording a finding that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. Insofar as disability:

The petitioner has contended that he has suffered multiple injuries and suffered permanent disability and to prove the same, he has produced certified copy of the wound certificate at Ex.P6 and discharge summaries at Exs.P7 to P9 and the disability certificate at Ex.P11.
We have perused Ex.P6.
As per Ex.P7- discharge card, the petitioner has taken treatment in the United Hospital, Kalaburagi as inpatient from 13.12.2018 to 30.01.2019 i.e., for 49 days.

As per Exs.P8 and P9, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:4941-DB petitioner was admitted at Gurunanak Hospital,
Bidar, as inpatient from 11.02.2019 to 22.02.2019 and 07.03.2019 to 11.03.2019 for removal of implants i.e., 17 days.
PW.2 has clinically examined PW.1 and found that the petitioner has sustained non-union femur with bone grafting and limb lengthening surgery.

The person in case of non-union supracondylar region left femur with implant in situ with malunited fracture proximal tibia with implant in situ with left knee arthritics with 5 inch shortening of left lower limb and has permanent physical impairment disability components.

5 inch shortening of left lower limb at 20%,
non-union of left femur (Supracondylar) at 20%, left knee ankylosis (no movements) at 15% and malunited fracture of proximal left tibia at 5%.
PW.2 has given total disability to the lower limb and whole body at 60%.
Further, the said doctor is a treated doctor.
The Tribunal hast taken 1/3rd of the disability assessed by PW.2 i.e., 20% which is on the lower side.

Considering the evidence of PW.2 and Ex.P11 i.e., disability certificate, we are of the view that the permanent disability NC:
2024:KHC-K:4941-DB suffered by the petitioner needs to be enhanced from 20% to 40%.
16. Insofar as quantum of compensation:

Though it is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner was doing business and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, however, in order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of proof of income, the Court has to assess the income as per the chart provided by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2018.
As per the chart, notional income of the petitioner would be Rs.11,750/- per month.

The petitioner is also entitled for addition of 40% towards future income in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. reported 2020 SCC Online SC 601.

(a) The appeal is allowed in part.
